Ticket: 20-second position feeds give empty tracks even with max_gap=30

Tracks built from a position feed with one report every 20 seconds come back almost entirely invalid (Path.valid is False nearly everywhere), even when I pass max_gap=30 to tracks.load_paths. Feeds with a report every 2 seconds are fine. Expected: with max_gap=30 a 20-second feed gives a fully valid track; with max_gap below 20 it should not.

The change:
--- a/jf/tracks.py
+++ b/jf/tracks.py
@@ -162,7 +162,7 @@
         t = np.asarray(t, float)
         i = np.clip(np.searchsorted(self.tp, t), 1, len(self.tp) - 1)
         gap = self.tp[i] - self.tp[i - 1]
-        return (t >= self.t0) & (t <= self.t1) & (gap <= 12.0)
+        return (t >= self.t0) & (t <= self.t1) & (gap <= self.max_gap)
 
     def pos(self, t):
         return self.sp(np.clip(np.asarray(t, float), self.t0, self.t1))


The regression test the engineer added:
import numpy as np

from jf import tracks


def test_load_paths_respects_max_gap(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    tp = np.arange(5, dtype=float) * 20.0
    tr = dict(
        flight="TEST", actype="B738", src="adsb_icao",
        tp=tp, lat=np.zeros(5), lon=tp, alt_geom=np.full(5, 10000.0),
        alt_baro=np.full(5, 10000.0), ground=np.zeros(5),
        p_coarse=np.zeros(5), tv=np.array([]), gs=np.array([]),
        track=np.array([]), vrate=np.array([]), v_coarse=np.array([]),
    )

    class Frame:
        def to_enu(self, lat, lon, alt):
            return np.stack((lon, lat, alt), axis=-1)

    monkeypatch.setattr(tracks, "load_snapshots", lambda path: {"abc123": tr})
    path = tmp_path / "feed.jsonl.gz"
    times = np.array([-1.0, 0.0, 10.0, 30.0, 70.0, 80.0, 81.0])

    paths, _ = tracks.load_paths(path, Frame(), max_gap=30.0)
    assert paths["abc123"].valid(times).tolist() == [False, True, True, True, True, True, False]

    paths, _ = tracks.load_paths(path, Frame(), max_gap=19.0)
    assert not paths["abc123"].valid(times).any()

    paths, _ = tracks.load_paths(path, Frame(), max_gap=20.0)
    assert paths["abc123"].valid(times[1:-1]).all()


Automated checks: new test passes; existing suite passes.

concerns: The fix changes the validity condition to use the instance attribute self.max_gap instead of a hardcoded 12.0 gap, which seems correct, but the test monkeypatches load_snapshots to return only one flight with fixed timestamps. This test only checks boolean validity but does not confirm that the tracks are correctly constructed with correct timestamps or handle edge cases properly.

The test inputs times with negative and out-of-range values but relies on clip inside pos(), not shown to be related to valid(). The logic in valid() uses searchsorted to find indexes which depend on self.tp; if self.tp is empty or improperly set, it may fail silently.

The regression test does not cover or assert the internal computed gap values or debug the positions of the search indices; it only asserts the valid() return values, which may mask deeper underlying issues if the gap calculation is wrong or if the original bug was caused by mismatch between max_gap in load_paths and this method’s use of self.max_gap.

No test is added to ensure that the actual gap values between consecutive points in self.tp respect max_gap or to check the complex scenario when times are exactly on boundaries, so the fix might hide symptoms rather than fixing root cause if other code uses different max_gap logic.
